sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `kiro`
- Canonical name: Kiro (`claim-kiro-nw-identity`)
- Current status: active; Web is preview; iOS is TestFlight early access; CLI 3.0 is early opt-in beside default 2.x (`claim-kiro-nw-status`, `claim-kiro-nw-status-web-preview`, `claim-kiro-nw-status-mobile-preview`, `claim-kiro-nw-status-cli-v3`)
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-17
- Vendor: AWS. Homepage: “Built and operated by AWS.” (`claim-kiro-nw-vendor`)
- Canonical URL: `https://kiro.dev/` (`claim-kiro-nw-canonical-url`)
- Repository: none published for IDE / CLI / Web (`claim-kiro-nw-repository-url`). Crew only: `https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew` (`claim-kiro-nw-repository-crew`). Do not write `https://github.com/kirodotdev/Kiro` as `repository_url`.
- Version: IDE 1.0.309 (`claim-kiro-nw-version-ide`). CLI 3.0 early; 2.x default (`claim-kiro-nw-version-cli`). CLI 2.18.1 dated 2026-08-14 (`claim-kiro-sf-version-cli-2-18-1`). Crew tag v0.2.0 (`claim-kiro-nw-version-crew`).
- Availability: country and region limits (`claim-kiro-nw-availability`)

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: one unified agent harness across IDE, CLI, Web, and Mobile (`claim-kiro-nw-what-it-is`). Spec-driven development with property-based tests (`claim-kiro-nw-what-it-is-specs`)
- What it is not: not a Visual Studio or Eclipse plugin (`claim-kiro-nw-not-for-vs-eclipse`); the iOS app is not the IDE or CLI (`claim-kiro-nw-not-for-ios-ide`); third-party automation harnesses are not permitted (`claim-kiro-nw-not-for-third-party-harness`); no first-party Android app (`claim-kiro-nw-not-for-android`); CLI 3.0 is not on Amazon Linux 2 (`claim-kiro-nw-not-for-al2`); no Free tier in GovCloud (`claim-kiro-nw-not-for-govcloud-free`)

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `ide` (`claim-kiro-nw-primary-type`). A standalone-harness reading exists as architecture only and is not a type flip (`claim-kiro-nw-primary-type-runtime-reading`)
- Secondary role: `cloud-agent` (`claim-kiro-nw-secondary-role`)
- Agent-loop owner: the Kiro harness owns the loop — a standalone process that orchestrates conversation, tools, context, permissions, and LLM providers (`claim-kiro-nw-agent-loop-owner`). Mapper-shaped value is `supported` (`claim-kiro-sf-loop-supported`)
- Architecture: ACP harness over stdio (local) and WebSocket (Web/Mobile); same binary (`claim-kiro-nw-architecture`). IDE based on Code OSS (`claim-kiro-nw-architecture-code-oss`). Config scopes `.kiro` plus `~/.kiro` (`claim-kiro-nw-architecture-config-scopes`)

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface ledger rows were not written this pass. First-party surfaces in prose:
  - Native desktop IDE (`claim-kiro-nw-surface-ide`)
  - Kiro CLI (`kiro-cli`) with an OS matrix (`claim-kiro-nw-surface-cli`, `claim-kiro-nw-surface-cli-matrix`)
  - Web at app.kiro.dev (`claim-kiro-nw-surface-web`)
  - Official first-party iOS TestFlight client (`claim-kiro-nw-surface-ios-docs`, `claim-kiro-nw-surface-ios-marketing`)
  - Crew local gateway workspace and seven messaging channels (`claim-kiro-nw-surface-crew`, `claim-kiro-nw-surface-crew-messaging`)
  - ACP clients: `kiro-cli acp`, JetBrains, Zed (`claim-kiro-nw-surface-acp`, `claim-kiro-nw-surface-jetbrains`, `claim-kiro-nw-surface-zed`)
- Execution location: same-device default for IDE/CLI (`claim-kiro-nw-execution-local`); vendor-cloud sandbox for Web/Mobile (`claim-kiro-nw-execution-cloud`); Crew on a user-controlled host with inference via kiro-cli (`claim-kiro-nw-execution-crew`)
- Platform compatibility: broad languages; GitHub and GitLab (`claim-kiro-nw-compatibility`). Web docs also name GitLab integration for adding a project and opening a merge request (`claim-kiro-sf-web-gitlab`)

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: catalog plus Auto on Amazon Bedrock (`claim-kiro-nw-model-strategy`). Three first-party lists disagree and are kept, not averaged: docs catalog (`claim-kiro-nw-model-catalog-docs`); FAQ exclusive-processing list ending at Opus 4.7 (`claim-kiro-nw-model-catalog-faq`); homepage image with a shorter multiplier set (`claim-kiro-nw-model-catalog-homepage-image`). Free card says Sonnet 4.5 (`claim-kiro-nw-model-free-card`); FAQ Free says Sonnet 4.6 (`claim-kiro-nw-model-free-faq`)
- Auth strategy: GitHub, Google, AWS Builder ID, IAM Identity Center, external IdP; CLI API keys (`claim-kiro-nw-auth-strategy`). AWS account not required (`claim-kiro-nw-auth-no-aws-account`). GovCloud: IdC or external IdP only (`claim-kiro-nw-auth-govcloud`)
- Provider support: Bedrock-served multi-provider (`claim-kiro-nw-provider-support`)
- BYOK: unknown. Existing row sits on `auth_strategy`, not `field=byok`. Opened models/auth pages do not establish operator-supplied OpenAI/Anthropic/`base_url` keys. `KIRO_API_KEY` is a Kiro subscription key (`claim-kiro-nw-byok`, `claim-kiro-sf-byok`)
- Local models: unknown. CLI voice uses local Whisper STT, which is not a local coding-model runtime. Existing row sits on `model_strategy`, not `field=local_models` (`claim-kiro-nw-local-models`, `claim-kiro-sf-local-models`)
- Subscription reuse: unknown. No first-party Claude/ChatGPT/Gemini subscription-reuse sentence. Identity SSO is not subscription reuse (`claim-kiro-sf-subscription-reuse`).

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: per-turn context assembly (`claim-kiro-nw-context-behavior`); 128K to 1M windows (`claim-kiro-nw-context-windows`)

- Session behavior: account-scoped cross-surface cloud sessions (`claim-kiro-nw-session-cloud`); checkpoints restore files — IDE supported, CLI experimental v2 (`claim-kiro-nw-session-checkpoints`); rewind forks the conversation, CLI only (`claim-kiro-nw-session-rewind`); `/tangent` side conversations (`claim-kiro-nw-session-tangent`)

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation is a split, not a single Yes/No. Cloud/Web: isolated sandbox (`claim-kiro-nw-isolation-cloud`). Local IDE default is not a sandbox — Supervised is a review workflow, not a permission boundary (`claim-kiro-nw-isolation-local`). Crew: OS sandbox; Windows fail-closed (`claim-kiro-nw-isolation-crew`). Capability tag records sandbox without collapsing the local cell (`claim-kiro-nw-tag-sandbox`)
- Permissions: `permissions.yaml` deny > ask > allow (`claim-kiro-nw-permissions`, `claim-kiro-nw-tag-permissions`, `claim-kiro-nw-tag-human-gates`)
- Security: HIPAA for IDE and CLI (`claim-kiro-nw-security-hipaa`); GovCloud with TLS 1.2+ (`claim-kiro-nw-security-enterprise`); paid output indemnity (`claim-kiro-nw-security-indemnity`)
- Data path: us-east-1 storage; cross-region inference (`claim-kiro-nw-data-path`). Service-improvement sharing unless opted out (`claim-kiro-nw-drawback-data-sharing`)

sections.body:
Surface ledger rows were not written this pass. Do not treat the prose names below as `surfaces.jsonl` IDs.

- Interface and surfaces in prose: IDE, CLI, Web, iOS, Crew, ACP clients as listed above (`claim-kiro-nw-surface-ide`, `claim-kiro-nw-surface-cli`, `claim-kiro-nw-surface-web`, `claim-kiro-nw-surface-ios-docs`, `claim-kiro-nw-surface-crew`, `claim-kiro-nw-surface-acp`)

No first-party Android app (`claim-kiro-nw-not-for-android`). sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: Free $0 / Pro $20 / Pro+ $40 / Pro Max $100 / Power $200, plus add-on credits at $0.04 (`claim-kiro-nw-pricing`). Enterprise dollar price unknown (`claim-kiro-nw-pricing-enterprise`)

sections.body:
### Source ledger

| Claim or record ID | Evidence class | Source URL | Captured/reviewed date | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claim-kiro-nw-*` (134 rows) | mixed official-claim / official-docs / repository-or-code | see each nw row | 2026-08-16 | accepted | Prior dense pack. Do not remint. |
| `claim-kiro-cmp-mobile` | official-claim | see row | 2026-08-16 | accepted | Compare mobile tag; official iOS app. |
| `claim-kiro-sf-license-ide-cli-aws-content` | official-docs | https://kiro.dev/license/ | 2026-08-17 | accepted | AWS Content for IDE and CLI |
| `claim-kiro-sf-version-cli-2-18-1` | official-docs | https://kiro.dev/changelog | 2026-08-17 | accepted | CLI 2.18.1 (2026-08-14) |

| `claim-kiro-sf-loop-supported` | official-docs | https://kiro.dev/docs/how-kiro-works/ | 2026-08-17 | accepted | Mapper-shaped agent_loop_owner=supported |
| `claim-kiro-sf-byok` | inference | https://kiro.dev/docs/models/ | 2026-08-17 | unreviewed | field=byok unknown; do not tag byok |
| `claim-kiro-sf-subscription-reuse` | inference | https://kiro.dev/docs/getting-started/authentication/ | 2026-08-17 | unreviewed | field=subscription_reuse unknown |
| `claim-kiro-sf-local-models` | inference | https://kiro.dev/docs/models/ | 2026-08-17 | unreviewed | field=local_models unknown; Whisper is STT |

### Unresolved contradictions (kept, not averaged)

- iOS 17+ (`claim-kiro-nw-ios-17`) vs iOS 26+ (`claim-kiro-nw-ios-26`)
- Model catalogs: docs vs FAQ (ends Opus 4.7) vs homepage image (`claim-kiro-nw-model-catalog-docs`, `claim-kiro-nw-model-catalog-faq`, `claim-kiro-nw-model-catalog-homepage-image`)
- Free model: Sonnet 4.5 card vs Sonnet 4.6 FAQ (`claim-kiro-nw-model-free-card`, `claim-kiro-nw-model-free-faq`)
- Web GitHub-required prerequisite vs GitLab integration feature (`claim-kiro-nw-surface-web`, `claim-kiro-sf-web-gitlab`)

### Compare-shaped (sourced vs unknown — not Yes/No)

- loop: sourced — harness owns the loop (`claim-kiro-nw-agent-loop-owner`, `claim-kiro-sf-loop-supported`). Mapper-shaped value is `supported` (`claim-kiro-sf-loop-supported`)
- sandbox: sourced as split — cloud yes (`claim-kiro-nw-isolation-cloud`); local IDE not sandboxed (`claim-kiro-nw-isolation-local`)
- byok: unsupported (`claim-kiro-cmp-byok`). Bedrock catalog; no operator-supplied keys. Older unknown rows stay on disk.
- local: left unknown (`claim-kiro-nw-local-models`, `claim-kiro-sf-local-models`). Whisper ≠ local coding model.
- sub: unsupported (`claim-kiro-cmp-subscription-reuse`). Own Kiro seats, not Claude/ChatGPT reuse.
- remote: sourced (`claim-kiro-nw-remote-access-cloud`, `claim-kiro-nw-tag-remote-control`)
- mobile: sourced supported — official iOS app (`claim-kiro-nw-mobile-access`, `claim-kiro-cmp-mobile`)
- license: sourced — AWS Content for IDE/CLI (`claim-kiro-sf-license-ide-cli-aws-content`) plus Crew Apache-2.0 (`claim-kiro-nw-license-crew`)
- pricing: sourced — Free $0 / Pro $20 / Pro+ $40 / Pro Max $100 / Power $200 (`claim-kiro-nw-pricing`)

sections.heading: Research note
sections.body: Thin keep-type write. `primary_type` stays `ide`. Mobile is the official iOS app. Star counts are not published. Surface ledger rows were not written.

claims.claim: Official models page presents a Kiro-served Bedrock catalog. It does not document operator-supplied OpenAI or Anthropic keys.
Official models page: Kiro is powered by Amazon Bedrock cross-region inference. No local Ollama or llama.cpp coding-model path is documented.
claims.notes: Compare local No. Whisper is not a coding model.

claims.claim: Kiro for iOS is an official native client in TestFlight early access.
claims.notes: Pointer to claim-kiro-nw-tag-native-ios. Leak close. Quote: "Kiro for iOS is available in early access through Apple TestFlight — request access to start and steer cloud sessions from your phone." Official iOS is enough for Yes. Re-verified 2026-08-17.

claims.claim: Official pricing is Kiro Free $0 / Pro $20 / Pro+ $40 / Pro Max $100 / Power $200 credit plans. Not Claude or ChatGPT consumer-plan reuse.
Privacy docs note Kiro supports Open VSX extensions including the community-maintained Open Remote - SSH extension.
claims.notes: Community, not first-party; no surface row.

claims.claim: The harness is a standalone process that orchestrates the conversation, executes tools, manages context, evaluates permissions, and talks to LLM providers.
The ACP page documents a JSON-RPC 2.0 machine interface over stdin/stdout.
claims.notes: Repair split; public REST sessions API unknown.

claims.claim: Headless mode needs KIRO_API_KEY and runs kiro-cli chat --no-interactive with CI examples.
Clients speak ACP: local clients over stdio, Web and Mobile over WebSocket to a sandboxed harness, same binary and tools.
FAQ says Kiro is based on Code OSS, allowing VS Code settings, themes, and Open VSX plugin import.
claims.notes: Code OSS is not a candidate id.

claims.claim: Project config lives in .kiro/, user config in ~/.kiro/, workspace trust under ~/.kiro/workspace-roots/<hash>/.
FAQ says GovCloud allows IAM Identity Center or external IdPs such as Okta and Entra ID, not GitHub, Google, or Builder ID.
claims.value: GovCloud IdC or external IdP only

claims.claim: FAQ says you do not need an AWS account to use Kiro.
Auth docs support GitHub, Google, Builder ID, IAM Identity Center, and external IdP across surfaces; API keys are CLI-only for CI on paid plans.
claims.value: social, Builder ID, IdC, external IdP; CLI API keys

claims.claim: FAQ limits individual paid plans to a published country list and names supported enterprise regions.
Web automations run a prompt against repositories on a schedule without the user starting a session.
How-Kiro-works says sessions keep running after the user closes the laptop.
Crew runs recurring jobs on a schedule and heartbeats that monitor systems until something needs attention.
Opened pages do not establish bring-your-own-key to a user-owned OpenAI or Anthropic account.
The first-party product site is https://kiro.dev/.
Compaction automatically summarizes older history near the model limit on all four surfaces; manual /compact is CLI-only.
FAQ lists supported languages including Python, Java, TypeScript, Go, Rust, C#, SQL, YAML, and HCL, and says the web agent coordinates GitHub and GitLab repos.
Each turn assembles the prompt, conversation so far, steering files, and attachments.
The models table lists per-model context windows from 128K to 1M.
Individual subscriber content is stored in US East (N. Virginia), enterprise content may sit in the profile region, and Bedrock cross-region inference routes traffic across listed regions.
Cloud sessions lack local-file affordances, Supervised mode, session renaming, and branch selection at attach.
Data-protection docs describe service improvement using individual content unless the user opts out, while some enterprise paths are excluded.
The Web Identity Center page says MCP registry URL and other governance policies such as model selection and web tool controls do not apply to Kiro Web, and customer managed keys are unsupported.
claims.notes: Repair split; page opened this pass.

claims.claim: Cloud sessions run the harness in a managed sandbox that clones repos server-side; the local working copy is not uploaded.
claims.notes: IDE v1.0.293+ and CLI v2.17+ to create or attach.

claims.claim: Crew runs its Gateway and sessions on user hardware while model requests are handled by kiro-cli.
IDE and CLI run the harness on the user machine by default with local filesystem, shell, and credentials.
FAQ says users can import VS Code settings, themes, and Open VSX compatible plugins.
The docs index describes Powers as tools with built-in knowledge that activate on demand.
The enterprise page advertises 90+ powers and an MCP server directory.
Hooks are v1 JSON files in .kiro/hooks/ triggered by events such as PostFileSave, PreToolUse, and Stop.
FAQ identifies Kiro as an agentic AI with an IDE, CLI, and web interface that turns prompts into specs, then code, docs, and tests.
The enterprise page targets teams needing AWS identity, governance, and subscription management.
The homepage says Kiro helps developers and teams turn prompts into executable specs and validate code.
The iOS page FAQ says Kiro for iOS requires a paid account and iOS 17+.
The same iOS page footer says the app requires iOS 26+ and a paid account.
The web sandbox is a secure isolated environment for agent execution, configurable from agent settings.
Crew README says kiro-cli can run in Linux namespace or macOS Seatbelt isolation and that Windows fails closed unless sandbox_allow_unsandboxed_exec is set.
Privacy docs say Supervised mode is a code review workflow, not a security control, so the local default is not a sandbox.
The KiroCrew LICENSE file is Apache License 2.0.
Opened pages publish no open-source license for the IDE, CLI, or web agent; they present an AWS commercial application.
claims.notes: Do not invent an SPDX id.

claims.claim: FAQ says Crew runs on the Kiro CLI using ACP and reads existing .kiro configuration, extending Kiro rather than replacing it.
claims.value: Crew extends Kiro CLI over ACP

claims.claim: No opened first-party page states that Kiro forks, wraps, or is built on another catalogue product; the Code OSS base and the Amazon Q Developer migration path are the only lineage statements found.
claims.notes: Repair: reviewer asked that the empty relationship ledger read as an evidence result, not silence. Checked research/data/candidates.csv on 2026-08-16: Code OSS and Amazon Q Developer have no candidate id, Kiro Crew shares the kiro id, and zed is a candidate id but hosts the Kiro agent, so an outbound kiro edge would face the wrong way.

claims.claim: AWS publishes a migration guide from Amazon Q Developer to Kiro; it is a successor path, not a stated fork.
claims.notes: Q Developer is not a candidate id.

claims.claim: Opened pages do not establish a first-party local coding-model runtime.
Docs page metadata shows dateModified 2026-08-14 for current pages checked two days later.
MCP availability: local stdio servers on IDE, CLI, and Web; remote HTTP/SSE and MCP config files on IDE and CLI only.
Crew persists sessions, memory, schedules, and task checkpoints beyond one chat and across Gateway restarts, turning corrections into durable lessons.
Steering files in .kiro/steering/ and ~/.kiro/steering/ give Kiro persistent project knowledge across sessions.
The documented mobile path is the iOS TestFlight app; no Android, mobile-web, or Termux route appears in mobile docs.
Models page lists GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, Claude Opus 5 and 4.8-4.5, Sonnet 5 and 4.6-4.0, Auto, Haiku 4.5, DeepSeek 3.2, MiniMax M2.5/M2.1, GLM-5, Qwen3 Coder Next.
FAQ says exclusive processing models are Sonnet 4.5, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.5, Opus 4.6, or Opus 4.7.

The homepage model-selector image carries first-party alt text naming the whole catalogue with credit multipliers: Auto at 1x; Claude Opus 4.8, 4.7, 4.6 and 4.5 at 2.2x; Claude Sonnet 4.6, 4.5 and 4 at 1.3x; Claude Haiku 4.5 at 0.4x; Deepseek v3.2 at 0.25x; and MiniMax M2.5 at 0.25x.
claims.notes: Residual fix pass 2026-08-16 (authorized by Maria, AI_OS/AUDITS/2026-08-16-next-wave-scope-decisions-receipt.md): the earlier row claimed the homepage catalogue was unreadable and recorded a research limit that does not exist. Reopened by public curl on 2026-08-16: the alt string appears twice on the page, including as imageAltText in the page data. This is a third model list beside model-catalog-docs and model-catalog-faq and now joins the model contradiction set.

claims.claim: Pricing Free card gives open weight models and Claude Sonnet 4.5, footnoting Qwen3 Coder Next, DeepSeek v3.2, MiniMax 2.1.
FAQ says the Free Tier includes open weight models and Claude Sonnet 4.6, with limits.
Models docs list a selectable catalog plus Auto with credit multipliers, served through Amazon Bedrock cross-region inference.
CLI 3.0 known gaps say CLI 3.0 does not run on Amazon Linux 2.
claims.notes: Repair split: only exclusion this page carries.

claims.claim: iOS marketing FAQ says Kiro is starting with iOS and will update if Android is supported later.
Pricing FAQ says the Free tier is not available in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions.
iOS marketing FAQ says the app manages agent sessions and is not the IDE or CLI.
claims.value: iOS app is not the IDE or CLI

claims.claim: FAQ says use through third-party automation harnesses such as OpenClaw that route requests outside Kiro native interfaces is not permitted.
Q-migration docs say Kiro has no native Visual Studio or Eclipse plugins.
Specs create requirements.md or bugfix.md, design.md, and tasks.md, then run tasks in dependency waves.
Custom agents can be invoked as sub-agents, and built-in context-gathering and general-purpose sub-agents handle delegated work.
claims.notes: Repair split. Web and Mobile use built-ins only.

claims.claim: IDE 1.0 Agent Focus Mode (experimental) runs several agents independently in multiple parallel sessions.
claims.notes: Repair split: sentence is on the IDE 1.0 page.

claims.claim: The main agent spawns sub-agents for parallelism, specialized tools, or context isolation and aggregates their results.
Running all spec tasks groups independent tasks into waves, starting with tasks that have no dependencies.
permissions.yaml at user and workspace scope sets deny, ask, and allow effects per capability, with deny winning.

claims.claim: Individual plans are Free $0/50 credits, Pro $20/1,000, Pro+ $40/2,000, Pro Max $100/5,000, Power $200/10,000, with add-on credits at $0.04 and GovCloud about 20% higher.
The enterprise page carries no dollar figure for enterprise or team plans.
claims.notes: Repair: reviewer listed enterprise and team dollar pricing as uncovered. Reopened by public curl 2026-08-16; the fetched page contains no price. Absence, not a denial that such pricing exists.
